h: Butterfly Tips and Island Days Out
p: Butterflies are at their liveliest when it's bright and warm, so a sunny morning often means more wings on the move in the tropical house. On duller days they tend to rest with their wings folded, which is actually a great chance to get close and study the patterns. Either way, move slowly, keep voices low and let them come to you. Bright clothing can sometimes attract a curious visitor or two.

If you're taking photos, turn off the flash and give your camera or phone a minute to adjust to the humidity, as lenses often steam up when you first walk in from the cold. Little ones should be reminded gently not to touch or grab, as butterfly wings are incredibly delicate.

Being close to the Menai Bridge end of the island, Pili Palas is a great starting point for an Anglesey day. Plas Newydd, the National Trust house and garden on the Menai Strait, has lovely grounds and views across to Snowdonia. Anglesey Sea Zoo at Brynsiencyn is a natural follow-on for more animal encounters, with creatures from the waters around the island.

Further west, Newborough beach and forest lead to Llanddwyn Island, a magical tidal spot with a lighthouse, sandy coves and views of the mountains. And of course you can't come this way without stopping for a photo at Llanfairpwll, the village with the famously long name, just a few minutes down the road.
